title: Quenched Melty Ukrainian Beef Tagine
description: A slow‑cooked, cheese‑pulling Ukrainian tagine that stays moist and flavorful, perfect for a halal‑friendly family dinner.
instructions: Heat the ceramic tagine over medium heat and add the olive oil.
Add the diced onion and minced garlic and sauté until the onion is translucent.
Stir in the ground cumin, coriander, paprika, salt, and pepper, cooking for one minute until fragrant.
Add the minced beef, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook until it starts to brown.
Pour in the tomato paste and stir to coat the beef evenly.
Add the diced carrot, bell pepper, tomato, beef broth, water, and bay leaf, then stir to combine.
Cover the tagine with its lid and reduce the heat to low, letting it simmer gently for 90 minutes.
Stir occasionally, ensuring the mixture stays moist and does not stick to the bottom.
Halfway through the cooking time, sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese over the top, then replace the lid and continue cooking until the cheese melts and pulls.
Once done, remove the tagine from heat, give the contents a final stir, and serve hot.
Garnish with chopped parsley before plating.
Cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 71°C / 160°F (no longer pink in the middle) before serving.
